headline: Inferring cell-state dynamics as distributions and paths from single-cell snapshots
label: Single Cell Computational Inference Methods
summary: Recent preprints and a March 2026 publication model single-cell and spatial snapshots as distributions, enabling trajectory and curvature-based inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is recovering dynamical and geometric structure from single-cell and spatial measurements that are typically static snapshots. MIOFlow 2.0 couples neural stochastic differential equations with unbalanced optimal transport growth rates to infer stochastic cellular trajectories from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics snapshots. Wasserstein Parallel Trends applies parallel transport on the Wasserstein manifold to counterfactual prediction of distributional dynamics. The published SCIM study embeds single-cell expression profiles as Gaussians under the Fisher metric and uses coarse Ricci curvature and RNA-velocity-derived information velocity to quantify phenotype transition manifolds. What is new is treating cell states as probability distributions or statistical manifolds, so transitions are modeled as paths, flows, or curvature rather than discrete state labels. The methods are distinct; the shared element is model-based inference over distributions rather than direct readout.
